bug_semantics: A template-controlled filter name was used as a bracket key on Liquid.filters, a normal JavaScript object. Therefore `valueOf` resolved to the inherited Object.prototype.valueOf even though no such filter had been registered. Filter.render then invoked that inherited function with an engine-owned receiver containing `context`, `liquid`, and, in later versions, `token`; valueOf returned the receiver itself. A crafted template could retain that object, traverse the leaked Liquid engine to its parser/loader/options/filesystem and filter registry, and use the advisory's group_by/where/comparable gadgets to obtain Function and invoke child_process, producing remote code execution. The analogous inherited lookup on Liquid.tags also let names such as `constructor` bypass the unknown-tag check. The fix makes both registries null-prototype objects so inherited Object.prototype members cannot resolve.
flaw_origin: The plain-object filter registry predated the vulnerability and the direct parent invoked filters with only a Context receiver. Commit f9f595f0f4604bfcfeabe097a01c6df6eb98baed is the smallest non-refactor commit that made the advisory's RCE-enabling leak: it deliberately threaded the complete Liquid instance through FilterMap/Value/Filter and changed src/template/filter/filter.ts from `this.impl.apply({ context }, ...)` to `this.impl.apply({ context, liquid: this.liquid }, ...)`. Because the inherited valueOf lookup already existed, that one focused feature commit made an unregistered template filter return a receiver containing the parser, filter registry, and filesystem-bearing engine. Later token exposure and group_by/where gadgets expanded or operationalized the attack but did not originate the privileged engine leak.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/security/advisories/GHSA-gf2q-c269-pqgc identifies CVE-2026-45618 and demonstrates `1|valueOf` returning the filter receiver, leakage of Context/Liquid internals, comparable-function gadgets, Function construction, and child_process execution. The maintainer's first-party fix thread https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/issues/897 states the exact root cause: `liquid.filters` and `liquid.tags` were plain `{}` objects; template-controlled bracket access inherited Object.prototype; src/template/filter.ts invoked the selected handler as `this.handler.apply({ context, token, liquid }, ...)`; and src/liquid.ts should use Object.create(null). History command `git log -L 27,35:src/template/filter.ts ... 457fae^` traces the privileged receiver back through renames and shows f9f595f0f4604bfcfeabe097a01c6df6eb98baed as the commit that first added `liquid: this.liquid`; `git show f9f595... -- src/liquid.ts src/template/filter/filter-map.ts src/template/filter/filter.ts` shows the focused propagation of Liquid into FilterMap and Filter and the changed apply receiver. Direct-parent verification at 2bbf50171be0ed484d9cb333f7d5a5dfca167486 shows src/template/filter/filter.ts still called `this.impl.apply({ context }, ...)`, Filter had no Liquid field or constructor argument, FilterMap accepted no Liquid instance, and src/liquid.ts constructed FilterMap with only strictFilters; thus the engine-leaking RCE mechanism is absent in the direct parent even though the older plain registry remains. At the BIC, src/liquid.ts declares public parser/filters/tags and private fs and passes `this` into FilterMap, confirming that the newly leaked object carries the privileged engine graph. `git cat-file -p f9f595...` proves one parent (not a merge/squash aggregate) and the exact human-only commit object. The advisory's first observable step is not merely a permissive unknown filter: it is inherited resolution of Object.prototype.valueOf followed by an invocation receiver that becomes template data. Plain registries existed earlier, so their later moves into src/liquid.ts are refactors rather than BICs. The causal history of Filter.render establishes the decisive boundary. Before f9f595, inherited valueOf was invoked with a receiver containing only Context; the direct parent contains no Liquid field or propagation path. f9f595 is a small feature commit specifically adding the whole Liquid instance to filter `this`; at that revision the leaked engine already contains parser, filters/tags, and fs. That is the first commit that writes the privileged-engine leak central to the RCE described by the maintainer. Later d705888c8d46d9dd95fcb41c0fb7bfbaf647eddd adds token to the same receiver and later filter additions supply convenient gadgets, but neither is the origin of the unsafe engine exposure. The lifecycle then persists through refactors, including the 2022 replacement of FilterMap with public plain registries, until direct fix 457fae switches both maps to null-prototype storage. Tag ancestry places f9f595 in the first affected release v9.17.0 and places 457fae first in v10.26.0, consistent with the patched boundary and the last-vulnerable v10.25.7 tree. Finally, only the BIC commit object was used for attribution: it is authored and committed by harttle and contains no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI. AI co-authorship visible on the much later fix is deliberately excluded from the BIC-only attribution decision.
